claims.text: Subjective uncertainty quantification and calibration in natural language generation can be formulated from a Bayesian decision theory perspective by defining utility as a similarity measure between a generated response and a hypothetical true response.
Epistemic uncertainty in natural language generation can be derived from a missing data perspective and characterized as excess risk.
The proposed Bayesian decision-theoretic uncertainty quantification methods can be applied to black-box language models.

evidence.description: This work addresses these challenges from a perspective of Bayesian decision theory, starting from the assumption that our utility is characterized by a similarity measure that compares a generated response with a hypothetical true response. We discuss how this assumption enables principled quantification of the model's subjective uncertainty and its calibration.
We further derive a measure for epistemic uncertainty, based on a missing data perspective and its characterization as an excess risk.
The proposed methods can be applied to black-box language models.

methodologies.name: Bayesian decision-theoretic subjective and epistemic uncertainty quantification
methodologies.description: A framework for quantifying subjective uncertainty calibration using similarity-based utility measures and deriving epistemic uncertainty as excess risk from a missing data perspective.

limitations.text: Uncertainty quantification in NLG free-form response generation is challenging due to the difficulty of defining task-specific uncertainties (such as semantic uncertainty) in general cases.
